item: #65 doubt 15 (2026-11-26): an OPENED long prompt is capped at 40% of the panel and scrolls inside itself, so the pinned bubble never hides the reply; folded (3 lines) and short prompts are unchanged
branch: css/25-turns.css .msg-user.fold.open (max-height var(--pin-max), overflow-y auto) · the token in css/00-tokens.css
provenance: No CLI frames claimed: the prompt is drawn with addUserMessage (draw-only) and the reply is an un-streamed assistant frame in the wire's shape (as fixture 119), with window.__bridge stubbed for the drawing so nothing reaches the CLI. MEASURED 2026-11-26 in the sandbox before the change: an 81-line prompt folded to 78px (9% of an 858px panel); opened, the pinned bubble covered 98, 98, 98, 100, 100, 88 and 77% of the panel along the reply's scroll. VS Code caps a pinned prompt at 40% of the panel (2.1.330 webview, read for the 2026-11-22 audit). NEGATIVE CONTROL 2026-11-26 against the sandbox on the pre-change CSS: the two DISCRIMINATING asserts failed (maxCover 100, no inner scroll), every GUARD passed. Draw and measure are separate steps because the fold and its click handler attach one animation frame after addUserMessage. First fixed-build run: the cap held (359px of an 897px panel = 40%) but the fixture divided by the log's own height (858px → 42%) and sampled every 200px of a now-shorter scroll; it now divides by window.innerHeight and samples every 100px.

GUARD: the opened state is set (the class the click toggles; set directly — the click handler attaches one animation frame after drawing, which raced the harness)
GUARD: the scroll walk really sampled the reply
DISCRIMINATING: opened, the pinned bubble covers at most 40% (+1 for rounding) of the panel (window.innerHeight: header, log and composer — what 40vh is) anywhere along the reply (pre-change: 100)
DISCRIMINATING: the rest of the prompt scrolls inside the bubble
GUARD: without the open class it is folded again
